The epitope-specific monoclonal scFv construct showed a preferential binding to A beta 1-42 fibrils. Oligomer binding was weaker. Signals for monomer binding were not detected if A beta 1-42 monomers were immobilized onto the streptavidin functionalized surface of the well via an N-terminal biotin tag, indicating interference of the N-terminal biotin tag with the binding of scFv-IC16 to the monomer.  A beta 1-42 monomers that were immobilized via a C-terminal biotin tag were bound by scFv.

Brain cryosections derived from nine or 12 months old transgenic (Tg 2576) mice expressing human amyloid beta and the respective non-transgenic control were stained using epitope-specific monoclonal scFv. The scFv detected plaques specifically in AD transgenic mice with low background signals.
Signals for binding were low if A beta 1-10 was immobilized onto the streptavidin functionalized surface of the well via an N-terminal biotin tag.

The epitope recognized by VHH KW1 was deduced based on reactivity on dot blots with overlapping peptides derived from Aß 1-42 (DAEFRHDSGYEVHHQKLVFFAEDVGSNKGAIIGLMVGGVVIA). Since KW1 binds to Aß 1-40 oligomers, the authors conclude that reactivity with some peptides may indicate an oligomerization of the recognized peptides. Oligomers made from Aß 1-40 with residues Va18l, Phe19, or Phe20 showed reduced or no binding of KW1. NMR studies also indicate that Aß 1-40 residues 15-24 and 31-37 interact with KW1.
The epitope specific VHH KW1 immunoprecipitated Aß 1-40 oligomers from Alzheimer's disease brain tissue, but not from tissue of a nondemented control.
The epitope specific VHH KW1 recognizes Aß 1-40 oligomers. NMR studies also indicate that Aß 1-40 residues 15-24 and 31-37, which include the epitope residues, interact with KW1.
The epitope-specific mAb stained the dense core amyloid plaques in APP/ PS mouse brains.
